title: High Velocity Transactions
content: Multiple transactions within a short time period (5+ in 1 hour) indicates potential card testing or account takeover. This pattern is commonly seen when fraudsters test stolen card credentials with small purchases before attempting larger transactions.

title: Device Fingerprint Changes
content: Sudden changes in device fingerprints, especially multiple devices in short succession, suggest compromised credentials. Legitimate users typically use 1-2 devices consistently.

title: MCC Risk Categories
content: High-risk MCCs include 5967 (teleservices), 7995 (gambling), 5966 (outbound marketing), 7273 (dating services). These categories have historically higher fraud rates and require additional scrutiny.

title: Chargeback Patterns
content: Customers with 2+ chargebacks in 6 months have 60% probability of future disputes. Enhanced monitoring recommended. Common chargeback reasons include unauthorized transactions, service not rendered, and product not received.

title: International Transaction Flags
content: International transactions, especially to high-risk countries, require verification. Impossible travel detection is key - transactions in different countries within physically impossible timeframes indicate fraud.

title: Card Freeze Guidelines
content: Freeze card immediately for risk scores >80 (critical), open dispute for 60-80 (high risk), contact customer for 40-60 (medium risk), monitor for <40 (low risk).

title: False Positive Indicators
content: Travel bookings, large purchases at known merchants, recurring subscriptions, and first-time large purchases often trigger false positives. Context matters - check merchant reputation and transaction history.

title: OTP Verification Requirements
content: Transactions >$500 or international transactions require OTP verification per PSD2/SCA requirements. Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) is mandatory in EU and recommended globally.

title: Amount Anomaly Detection
content: Transactions 3x or more above customer's average spending are flagged. Consider transaction type and merchant category. Large purchases at luxury retailers may be legitimate during holidays.

title: Time-based Risk Factors
content: Transactions between midnight and 5 AM have 40% higher fraud rates. Weekend and holiday transactions also show elevated risk. Combine with other signals for accurate assessment.
